sources.entry: LLDAP | Lightweight LDAP server for user management

summary.one_liner: lldap is a lightweight LDAP-based authentication server with a web UI for managing users and groups, aimed at self-hosted services that only support LDAP.
summary.what_it_does: lldap provides a simplified LDAP interface for authentication, intentionally not a full LDAP server. It includes a web frontend for creating users, setting passwords, managing groups, and letting users edit their own details or reset passwords by email (when SMTP is configured). Custom attributes can be managed through the web UI or a community CLI. A bootstrap.sh script can enforce a list of users, groups, and attributes from a file, and the server is scriptable through a GraphQL API. Data is stored in SQLite by default, with MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL as alternatives. Installation options named include OCI images (docker/podman), Kubernetes, TrueNAS, distribution packages, and building from source.
use_cases: central user management for self-hosted apps
LDAP authentication for Nextcloud or Airsonic
single source of truth for users feeding Authelia or KeyCloak
managing LDAP users and groups through a web UI
automating user and group setup from a file
managing users as code with a terraform provider
how_to_run: Install via OCI image (docker/podman), Kubernetes, TrueNAS, or a distribution package manager
Or build from source with cargo
Configure the default admin DN cn=admin,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com and password in the configuration
Point services at LLDAP's LDAP port using the documented DN layout (ou=people, ou=groups)
Optionally run bootstrap.sh with a file to enforce users, groups, and attributes
notable: Opinionated, simplified LDAP interface that avoids needing to understand slapd or full LDAP complexity
Web UI for user self-service, including password reset by email
Dedicated groups (lldap_strict_readonly, lldap_password_manager) for limiting service access
Scriptable through a GraphQL API and an infrastructure-as-code terraform provider
caveats: Not a full LDAP server; many LDAP browsing tools and features are unsupported
Services that require password hashes for local validation are incompatible, including Synology
Windows/Samba integration is described as work in progress
